name: Kappa
summary: Mischievous, turtle-backed river dwellers that bargain with humans in exchange for cucumbers or favors.
summaryJa: 川や沼に棲む、亀の甲羅を背負った悪戯好きの水の妖怪。頭の皿の水が力の源で、キュウリと相撲が大好物。
legends: Challenges travellers to sumo bouts by the water's edge
Known to return politeness with politeness, sometimes to their own downfall
Steals shirikodama from swimmers who linger at the river
If you bow deeply to a kappa, it will bow back and spill the life-giving water from its sara (head dish).
traits: Dish of water on the crown
funFact: If you bow deeply to a kappa, it will bow back and spill the life-giving water from its sara (head dish).
funFactJa: 河童に深くお辞儀をすると、律儀にお辞儀を返して頭の皿の水をこぼしてしまうという。
searchQuery: 河童 妖怪 民話
creativeHooks: Imagine a riverside festival game inspired by a kappa's playful pranks.
Design a collaborative truce between local farmers and a curious kappa.
A municipal treaty written in cucumbers and sumo rules.

name: Tengu
region: Mountain shrines and deep cedar forests
summary: Avian-nosed martial spirits who guard sacred mountains and challenge arrogant wanderers.
summaryJa: 高い鼻と翼を持つ山の護り手。慢心した旅人や僧を懲らしめ、見込んだ者には剣術を授けるという。
legends: Teaches swordplay to worthy disciples
Kidnaps boastful priests to humble them
Abducts arrogant priests and returns them humbled as tengu-kakushi
Some medieval stories claim tengu invented the fan that can summon storms with a single flap.
traits: Long nose or beak and fan of wind
funFact: Some medieval stories claim tengu invented the fan that can summon storms with a single flap.
funFactJa: 一振りで嵐を呼ぶ羽団扇は天狗の発明だと語る中世の物語もある。
searchQuery: 天狗 修験道 伝承
creativeHooks: Stage a duel where a tengu tests a traveller's resolve atop a precarious bridge.
Create a secret tengu dojo hidden behind masked cedar trees.
A dojo whose headmaster is the mountain.

name: Yuki-onna
summary: Ethereal women cloaked in frost who appear during blizzards, balancing mercy and chill judgment.
summaryJa: 吹雪の夜に現れる氷のように美しい女性の妖怪。慈悲と冷徹さをあわせ持ち、心優しい者を見逃すこともある。
legends: Spare kind-hearted woodcutters who share warmth
Vanish at sunrise, leaving only drifting snowflakes
Lets a woodcutter live if he never tells he met her; the wife is the oath
Some tales describe the Yuki-onna carrying a baby made of ice to test a traveller's compassion.
funFact: Some tales describe the Yuki-onna carrying a baby made of ice to test a traveller's compassion.
funFactJa: 旅人の情けを試すため、氷でできた赤子を抱いて現れるという言い伝えも残る。
searchQuery: 雪女 逸話 民俗学
creativeHooks: Compose a scene where a Yuki-onna negotiates a fragile truce with spring itself.
Illustrate snowflake sigils that mark the path to a Yuki-onna's hidden glade.
A household whose thermostat is a vow.

name: Kitsune
summary: Shape-shifting fox spirits credited with trickery, wisdom, and occasionally saving entire provinces.
summaryJa: 変化と幻術を操る狐の霊。悪戯もすれば知恵で国を救いもする、稲荷神の使いとしても知られる存在。
legends: Transforms into a dazzling performer to expose corruption
Serves as messengers to the deity Inari
Serves a court as Tamamo-no-Mae until the tails show
Folklore says each tail a kitsune grows grants a century of experience and sharpens its magic.
funFact: Folklore says each tail a kitsune grows grants a century of experience and sharpens its magic.
funFactJa: 尻尾が一本増えるごとに百年分の経験と、より強い妖力が宿るとされる。
searchQuery: 九尾狐 伝説 稲荷
creativeHooks: Imagine a kitsune producing illusions to orchestrate a moonlit festival.
Plot a political thriller where a kitsune advisor balances trickery with loyalty.
A cabinet minister with a den under the palace.

name: Bakeneko
region: Castle towns and tea houses across Japan
summary: Once-domestic cats who, after long years, gain the uncanny ability to mimic human life and speech.
summaryJa: 長い年月を生きた飼い猫が化けたもの。人の言葉を話し、手ぬぐいを被って踊るなど、人間の暮らしを真似る。
legends: Disguises itself as an innkeeper to run a midnight salon
Dances with a towel wrapped on its head in the glow of lantern light
Dances with a napkin on its head when the house sleeps
People once believed a cat's tail should be shortened to prevent it from becoming a bakeneko.
funFact: People once believed a cat's tail should be shortened to prevent it from becoming a bakeneko.
funFactJa: 猫が化け猫にならないよう、尻尾を短く切る風習があったと伝えられる。
searchQuery: 化け猫 怪談 江戸
creativeHooks: Script a late-night tea ceremony hosted by a refined bakeneko.
Invent a jazz club run by century-old cats trading gossip for secrets.
A kitchen that unionised without the cook.

name: Nurikabe
summary: Invisible wall yokai that halts travellers, forcing them to rethink their route or wait until dawn.
summaryJa: 夜道で突然行く手を阻む見えない壁の妖怪。棒で足元を払うと消えるが、上の方を叩いても効かないという。
legends: Blocks the path of impatient samurai, yet lets lost children pass
Said to fade if tapped with a stick near the ground
Blocks the road as a wall; walking through it is the only key
Some Edo-period maps warn, tongue-in-cheek, of nurikabe hotspots to explain mysteriously long journeys.
funFact: Some Edo-period maps warn, tongue-in-cheek, of nurikabe hotspots to explain mysteriously long journeys.
funFactJa: 江戸時代には、旅がやけに長引いた言い訳として「ぬりかべの仕業」と冗談めかして語られたという。
searchQuery: ぬりかべ 伝説 道中
creativeHooks: Design an escape-room puzzle where the walls are mischievous nurikabe spirits.
Write a travelogue that becomes an allegory about embracing detours.
Urban planning that is a monster.

name: Rokurokubi
summary: By day they appear human; by night their necks stretch impossibly long, roaming halls in search of stories.
summaryJa: 昼間は普通の人間に見えるが、夜になると首が伸びて家中を徘徊する妖怪。行灯の油を舐めるとも噂される。
legends: Eavesdrops on sleeping guests to devour their whispered secrets
Falls for a traveller who notices her dual life
The neck tours the rafters while the body stays in bed
Old tales describe rokurokubi sending their heads to scout ahead while the body continues household chores.
funFact: Old tales describe rokurokubi sending their heads to scout ahead while the body continues household chores.
funFactJa: 体が家事を続けている間に、首だけを先へ偵察に飛ばすというろくろ首の話も残っている。
searchQuery: ろくろ首 怪異 怪談
creativeHooks: Compose a mystery solved by a rokurokubi who hears clues in the rafters.
Storyboard a comic where elongated necks become a whimsical superpower.
A CCTV system made of vertebrae.

name: Umibozu
summary: Enigmatic, towering figures that rise from turbulent seas, tipping ships unless appeased with lantern light.
summaryJa: 荒れた海から突如現れる黒く巨大な坊主頭の怪異。船を沈めるが、灯りや油を捧げると鎮まるという。
legends: Silences entire crews before crushing their masts
Seeks offerings of oil to calm the waves
Demands barrels from ships; a bottomless cask buys the tide
Fisherfolk once feared whispering the umi-bozu's name, believing it summoned waves tall enough to swallow lighthouses.
funFact: Fisherfolk once feared whispering the umi-bozu's name, believing it summoned waves tall enough to swallow lighthouses.
funFactJa: 海坊主の名を口にするだけで灯台を飲み込むほどの大波が来ると信じ、漁師たちはその名を囁くことさえ恐れた。
searchQuery: 海坊主 海難 民話
creativeHooks: Plot a maritime negotiation between lighthouse keepers and a lonely umi-bozu.
Create ambient sea shanties that keep the umi-bozu lulled to sleep.
A harbour fee collected in person.

name: Gashadokuro
summary: Gigantic skeleton spirits formed from the restless dead, stalking the countryside until pacified with ritual bells.
summaryJa: 戦や飢饉で弔われなかった死者の骨が集まってできた巨大な骸骨。深夜に現れ、耳鳴りがその接近の合図とされる。
legends: Materializes at midnight to devour lone travellers
Announced by a ringing in the ears before it strikes
Assembles from the unburied bones of a starved field
Some modern retellings convert the gashadokuro into gentle guardians once their bones are respectfully enshrined.
funFact: Some modern retellings convert the gashadokuro into gentle guardians once their bones are respectfully enshrined.
funFactJa: 現代の再話には、骨を丁重に祀れば村の守り神に変わるという優しい結末も生まれている。
searchQuery: 餓者髑髏 怪物 伝説
creativeHooks: Write a requiem that persuades a gashadokuro to become a village protector.
Design glowing talismans that disrupt the skeleton's eerie ear-ringing omen.
A memorial that stands up and walks.

name: Amabie
summary: A mermaid-like oracle who surfaces to warn of plagues and promises good harvests if its image is shared.
summaryJa: 海から現れて疫病を予言し、「私の姿を描き写して人に見せよ」と告げたと伝わる熊本の予言獣。
legends: Emerges shining from the sea to deliver prophecies
Inspires villagers to sketch its likeness for protection
Asks to be drawn and shown to ward plague
During modern outbreaks, Japanese artists revived the tradition of drawing Amabie as a charm against illness.
funFact: During modern outbreaks, Japanese artists revived the tradition of drawing Amabie as a charm against illness.
funFactJa: 令和の感染症流行時には、姿を描いて共有する「アマビエチャレンジ」としてSNSで復活した。
searchQuery: アマビエ 予言 疫病
creativeHooks: Curate a community mural project led by Amabie fans across eras.
Imagine Amabie livestreaming predictions to lighthouse keepers.
A public-health poster that talks back.

name: Zashiki-warashi
region: Old family homes of Tohoku, especially Iwate
summary: Childlike guardian spirits dwelling in tatami rooms, showering fortune on households that treat them kindly.
summaryJa: 座敷や蔵に棲みつく童子姿の家神。住み着いた家には幸運をもたらすが、去られると家運が傾くと伝わる。
legends: Leaves tiny footprints in scattered ashes overnight
Fortune follows the household it inhabits and fades when it departs
Leaves when the house grows cruel; fortune follows the child out
Some inns in Iwate keep rooms where guests hope to glimpse a zashiki-warashi, with bookings stretching years ahead.
traits: Red or white child in the parlor
funFact: Some inns in Iwate keep rooms where guests hope to glimpse a zashiki-warashi, with bookings stretching years ahead.
funFactJa: 岩手県には座敷童子に会えると評判の旅館があり、その部屋は数年先まで予約が埋まるほどの人気だという。
searchQuery: 座敷童子 岩手 伝承
creativeHooks: Write a family drama where renovating an old home risks evicting its zashiki-warashi.
Design a cozy game about earning the trust of an unseen playmate room by room.
A vacancy that is a credit rating.

name: Nue
summary: A chimera with a monkey's face, tanuki's body, tiger's limbs, and serpent tail whose night cry heralded misfortune at court.
summaryJa: 猿の顔、狸の胴、虎の手足、蛇の尾を持つ怪鳥。夜ごと帝を悩ませ、源頼政に射落とされた『平家物語』の怪異。
legends: Tormented Emperor Konoe beneath black clouds until Minamoto no Yorimasa shot it from the night sky
Its body was set adrift down the river in a dugout boat to carry the curse away
Cries over the palace until Yorimitsu's arrow finds it
The nue is named for a real bird, the scaly thrush, whose mournful night call was itself considered an evil omen.
funFact: The nue is named for a real bird, the scaly thrush, whose mournful night call was itself considered an evil omen.
funFactJa: 「ぬえ」の名は夜に物悲しく鳴く鳥トラツグミに由来し、正体不明の人物を指す「鵺的」という言葉まで生んだ。
searchQuery: 鵺 平家物語 退治
creativeHooks: Compose a courtly mystery where an unseen cry sickens the capital night after night.
Reimagine the nue as a misunderstood patchwork creature searching for its true form.
A noise complaint filed with a bow.

name: Kamaitachi
region: Snowy plains of the Koshin'etsu region
summary: Sickle-clawed weasels riding whirlwinds in trios — one topples, one cuts, one salves — leaving painless wounds behind.
summaryJa: つむじ風に乗って現れるイタチの妖怪。三匹一組で、転ばせ、切りつけ、薬を塗って去るため、傷は痛まないという。
legends: Rides whirlwinds as a trio: the first knocks travellers down, the second cuts, the third heals
Blamed for mysterious painless gashes that appear after cold gusts
Cuts in a trio of wind: knock-down, slice, plaster
In some regions people carried old calendars as charms, believing the paper could ward off kamaitachi cuts.
funFact: In some regions people carried old calendars as charms, believing the paper could ward off kamaitachi cuts.
funFactJa: 地方によっては古暦を懐に入れておくと鎌鼬の切り傷を防げるという、紙のお守りの風習があった。
searchQuery: 鎌鼬 つむじ風 伝承
creativeHooks: Choreograph a heist executed by three weasel spirits within a single gust of wind.
Sketch a rivalry between a kamaitachi trio and a modern wind-turbine town.
A street fight conducted by weather.

name: Ittan-momen
summary: A ten-metre strip of white cotton that flutters through dusk skies and wraps itself around late-night walkers.
summaryJa: 夕暮れの空をひらひらと飛ぶ一反（約10メートル）の白い木綿。夜道を歩く人の顔に巻きつくと伝わる鹿児島の妖怪。
legends: Flutters out of the dusk to wrap around the faces of night walkers
Kagoshima tales say it can be repelled with a blade or a well-timed bite
Wraps a night walker and flies them off the road
GeGeGe no Kitaro recast the ittan-momen as a heroic flying companion, making it one of Japan's best-loved yokai.
funFact: GeGeGe no Kitaro recast the ittan-momen as a heroic flying companion, making it one of Japan's best-loved yokai.
funFactJa: 『ゲゲゲの鬼太郎』では鬼太郎たちを乗せて空を飛ぶ頼れる仲間として描かれ、一躍人気者になった。
searchQuery: 一反木綿 鹿児島 妖怪
creativeHooks: Draft an aerial courier service run by reformed ittan-momen.
Animate a bolt of cloth learning to be a hero's cape instead of a prankster.
A kimono shop with a flight path.

name: Amanojaku
region: Temple gates and mountain passes across Japan
summary: A perverse imp that reads hearts and goads people into doing the opposite of their true wishes.
summaryJa: 人の心を読み、わざと逆のことをさせようとするひねくれ者の小鬼。仏堂では四天王像に踏みつけられる姿で知られる。
legends: Provokes people into blurting out hidden desires, then twists them
In the tale of Uriko-hime, it deceives and impersonates the melon princess
Does the opposite of every order, including 'don't save us'
Amanojaku lives on in everyday Japanese: calling someone an 'amanojaku' still means they are a natural contrarian.
funFact: Amanojaku lives on in everyday Japanese: calling someone an 'amanojaku' still means they are a natural contrarian.
funFactJa: ひねくれ者を指す「あまのじゃく」という言葉として、現代の日常会話にも生き続けている。
searchQuery: 天邪鬼 民話 瓜子姫
creativeHooks: Write a negotiation where the only way to win is to wish for the opposite.
Design a puzzle boss that mirrors and inverts the player's every choice.
A compliance officer who only fails.

name: Nopperabou
region: Roads and lonely paths across Japan
summary: A human-shaped apparition whose face is a blank expanse of skin, startling travellers who expect ordinary features.
summaryJa: 人の姿をしながら顔がのっぺりと平面の妖怪。道で声をかけた相手が振り向くと、そこには顔がない。
legends: Appears as a familiar stranger before revealing its blank face
Sometimes a second nopperabou waits further down the road
A second faceless person confirms the first was not a dream
Many classic kaidan end with the horrified traveller meeting another faceless figure at home or at an inn.
funFact: Many classic kaidan end with the horrified traveller meeting another faceless figure at home or at an inn.
funFactJa: 家に逃げ帰っても、待っていた家族や宿の主人まで顔がない、という落ちの怪談が多い。
searchQuery: のっぺらぼう 怪談
creativeHooks: Write a mystery where only reflections still have faces.
Design a city whose citizens gradually lose their features overnight.
A login screen with no fields.

name: Akaname
summary: A long-tongued yokai that creeps into dirty bathrooms to lick up grime, a living caution for unclean places.
summaryJa: 長い舌で風呂や不潔な場所の垢を舐める妖怪。清潔を怠ると現れる、という戒めでもある。
legends: Licks the scum from uncleaned bathtubs after midnight
Startles householders who leave damp corners neglected
Licks the scum from the bath after the house sleeps
The name literally means 'filth licker,' tying the monster directly to household cleanliness lore.
funFact: The name literally means 'filth licker,' tying the monster directly to household cleanliness lore.
funFactJa: 名前そのものが「垢を嘗める」意味で、家の衛生譚と直結している。
searchQuery: 垢嘗 妖怪 風呂
creativeHooks: Stage a haunted sento where the akaname is the only honest cleaner.
Turn a cleanliness campaign into a pact with a shy akaname.
A cleaning contract that is a mouth.

name: Chochin-obake
summary: An aged paper lantern that sprouts a single eye and a lolling tongue, laughing as it floats through the dark.
summaryJa: 古びた提灯が目と長い舌を生やして浮かぶ付喪神。夜道や祭りの灯りに紛れて現れる。
legends: Bursts into cackling flame-light on deserted streets
Joins processions of other animated tools
Splits its paper and shows one eye on a festival street
It is among the most iconic tsukumogami designs in ukiyo-e and modern yokai art.
funFact: It is among the most iconic tsukumogami designs in ukiyo-e and modern yokai art.
funFactJa: 浮世絵から現代の妖怪画まで、付喪神の代表的なビジュアルとして親しまれている。
searchQuery: 提灯お化け 付喪神
creativeHooks: Animate a lantern parade that judges which festivals still remember old tools.
Design a comedy duo of chochin-obake and karakasa-obake.
A lantern that files a complaint.

name: Karakasa-obake
summary: A tattered oil-paper umbrella that hops on one leg, often with a single eye and a long tongue.
summaryJa: 古い和傘が一本足でぴょんぴょん跳ねる付喪神。一つ目に長い舌が定番の姿。
legends: Hops after people on rainy nights
Startles passers-by then totters away laughing
Hops on one foot in the rain, tongue out, unused
Also called kasa-obake; one of the friendliest faces of the tsukumogami tradition.
funFact: Also called kasa-obake; one of the friendliest faces of the tsukumogami tradition.
funFactJa: 「傘おばけ」とも呼ばれ、付喪神のなかでも親しみやすい人気者。
searchQuery: 唐傘お化け 付喪神
creativeHooks: Write a rainy-day courier service run by karakasa-obake.
Illustrate a repair shop where broken umbrellas apply to become yokai.
Lost-and-found that patrols.

name: Bake-danuki
summary: Racoon-dog spirits famed for belly-drum illusions, transformation, and bawdy humour.
summaryJa: 腹鼓や変化で人を化かす狸の妖怪。徳島の金長狸など、地方英雄譚にも登場する。
legends: Transforms leaves into fake money or houses
Drums its belly to create illusions under the moon
Pays at an inn with leaves that are coins until morning
Unlike the often elegant kitsune, tanuki lore leans comic, earthy, and mercantile.
funFact: Unlike the often elegant kitsune, tanuki lore leans comic, earthy, and mercantile.
funFactJa: 狐が知的・神秘的に描かれがちなのに対し、狸は滑稽で商売上手なイメージが強い。
searchQuery: 化け狸 伝説 金長
creativeHooks: Plot a merchant war between a bake-danuki and a kitsune banker.
Design a festival float powered by tanuki belly-drums.
A fintech that photosynthesises.

name: Nekomata
summary: An elder cat whose tail splits in two as it gains supernatural power, sometimes raising the dead or speaking human words.
summaryJa: 長い歳月を経て尻尾が二股に裂けた猫の妖怪。人語を話し、死者を操るとも伝えられる。
legends: Dances with a towel on its head like a bakeneko
Commands corpses or curses ungrateful households
The forked tail comes with years; the hearth cat outlives the family
Folklore often links nekomata to cats kept too long, feeding fear and reverence for old felines.
funFact: Folklore often links nekomata to cats kept too long, feeding fear and reverence for old felines.
funFactJa: 飼い猫を長く飼うことへの畏れと敬意が、猫又譚には色濃く残る。
searchQuery: 猫又 妖怪 伝承
creativeHooks: Write a mountain tea house run by a refined nekomata medium.
Stage a court case where a nekomata testifies for its late owner.
A pensioner with two tails and a grudge.

name: Kodama
summary: Spirits dwelling in ancient trees; harming their host tree invites eerie echoes and misfortune.
summaryJa: 老木に宿る精霊。宿主の木を傷つけると山彦のような怪異や祟りがあるとされる。
legends: Returns a climber's call as an uncanny echo
Marks sacred trees that villagers refuse to cut
Echoes a woodcutter until the tree is asked, not taken
The word also simply means the echo in the mountains, blurring spirit and natural phenomenon.
funFact: The word also simply means the echo in the mountains, blurring spirit and natural phenomenon.
funFactJa: 「木霊」は山の木魂であると同時に、山彦（こだま）現象の名でもある。
searchQuery: 木霊 妖怪 森林
creativeHooks: Design a logging drama where every felled tree releases a kodama contract.
Compose a silent forest level where only kodama echoes guide the player.
A logging permit issued by the tree.

name: Yamauba
summary: An old woman of the deep mountains who may devour travellers—or foster heroes and share secret knowledge.
summaryJa: 深山に住む老女の妖怪。人を喰らう恐怖の存在でもあり、英雄を育て知恵を授ける面もある。
legends: Offers shelter then reveals monstrous hunger
Raises abandoned children into legendary warriors
Feeds a hero, then shows the mouth that could eat him
Some traditions link yamauba to childbirth deities and spinning, not only cannibal terror.
funFact: Some traditions link yamauba to childbirth deities and spinning, not only cannibal terror.
funFactJa: 産育や機織りと結びつく伝承もあり、単なる人食い鬼婆に留まらない。
searchQuery: 山姥 民話 山
creativeHooks: Write a yamauba midwife who prices her aid in years of memory.
Retell a hero origin as a reluctant apprenticeship to a yamauba.
A B&B whose terms of service are hunger.

name: Oni
summary: Horned, fang-mouthed beings of immense strength—villains of Setsubun, guardians of hell, and symbols of raw power.
summaryJa: 角と牙、虎柄のパンツが典型の鬼。節分の悪役、地獄の獄卒、力の象徴と多面的に語られる。
legends: Driven out with roasted soybeans at Setsubun
Serves as underworld jailers or mountain bandits
Driven out at Setsubun with beans, then hired as a gate god
Calling someone an 'oni' can mean cruel villain or awe-inspiring tough person, depending on tone.
funFact: Calling someone an 'oni' can mean cruel villain or awe-inspiring tough person, depending on tone.
funFactJa: 「鬼のような」は冷酷さも、畏れ多い強さも表せる両義的な言葉。
searchQuery: 鬼 民話 節分
creativeHooks: Reimagine Setsubun from the oni side of the door.
Design an oni blacksmith who forges clubs that only the pure can lift.
Seasonal contractors with clubs.

name: Shuten-doji
summary: A sake-loving oni chieftain who abducted nobles until Minamoto no Raiko's band defeated him.
summaryJa: 酒を愛する鬼の頭領。京の姫をさらい、源頼光一行に大江山で討たれたと伝えられる。
legends: Feasts on captives atop Mount Ooe
Is tricked by poisoned sake and divine disguises
Drinks poisoned sake on Oe-yama and still bites the lid of the box
